output.text: The morning fog had barely lifted when the volunteers gathered near the pier for the beach clean-up. Otto arrived first, stretching his arms and greeting everyone with a wide grin. Kira showed up a few minutes later, carrying a stack of mesh bags for collecting debris. Assume that Cleo is the head judge. Esme trailed in last, still tying her shoelaces as she jogged across the sand. Leo waved from the boardwalk, balancing a cooler and a clipboard in his arms. The five of them split into small groups to cover different sections of the shoreline, each armed with gloves and buckets. Leo brought the first-aid kit. Cleo, who was slightly taller than Kira but shorter than Otto, wandered along the tide line noting how much trash had washed up overnight. Otto finished ahead of Kira. As the sun rose higher, the group began sorting their collected items into recycling bins and trash bags. Kira finished ahead of Esme. Esme, the youngest of the group, laughed as she found an old flip-flop buried in the sand. Otto finished ahead of Esme. By midday, the beach looked remarkably cleaner, with neat piles of sorted waste lined along the boardwalk. Leo, who was the oldest among them, took a moment to photograph the results for the community newsletter. Everyone agreed that the clean-up had been a great success, and they made plans to return the following month to continue their work along the coastline.
